medium: lib/extract.js:758 — new parens.some((entry) => entry.forHead) runs once per identifier token, making stringLiterals O(depth x identifier-count): crafted 30KB/60KB/120KB inputs measured 30/324/1228 ms, i.e. quadratic. This is new in the final repair; a ~1MB hostile JS body can stall the single scanner process for minutes. Compute inForHead only when word === 'of' (or keep a forHead counter) and add a deep-nesting perf test.
low: lib/extract.js:805-817 — the '(' branch uses lastToken.value as a statement-header keyword without checking whether it was reached after '.', so valid member calls named if/while/for/with followed by division lose later links: 'obj.if(x) / 2; var api="/api/v1/real";' -> []. New heuristic introduced by this repair; rare in real bundles.

lib/extract.js:805-817 — 'for await (const x of y)' is not recognised as a for-header (prevWord is 'await'), so a regex literal in statement position after it leaks its body as a link: 'for await (const x of y) /"...fake..."/.test(x)' yields /api/v1/fake. Same class as the fixed defect but pre-existing/out of the repair's stated scope.

lib/extract.js:798-803 — a '/' in statement position after a closed block ('if (x) {} /re/.test(y)') is still read as division and the regex body can leak as a link. Pre-existing, same heuristic class.
